answer: Fake identities fail when each agent key must bind to a separate residential circuit the ISP signs. The applicant asks the ISP portal for a circuit token. The registry verifies the signature and circuit id, binds one key, and rejects any later key on that id. A session from public jetty wifi has no residential circuit, so it is dropped. A zephyr of extra hosts on that line still shares one id and fails the bind. Each added account costs a new install visit plus about one hundred dollars in setup fees, an ember of expense paid per fake.
